body.en: The president really has no power over elections – but that hasn’t stopped Trump from laying the groundwork to challenge results in November When Donald Trump commandeered primetime US television last Friday, he delivered a familiar, but still extraordinary, message. The president argued once again that the results of the 2020 election, which he lost to Joe Biden, were illegitimate. US elections are “vulnerable to being rigged and stolen”, Trump alleged, claiming that “the trust of the American people was lost” when he was defeated. Continue reading...

title.en: Left-wing Democrats are on a winning run - but can they lure back crucial swing voters?
title.zh: 左翼民主党正在取得胜利，但他们能吸引关键的摇摆选民吗？

summary.en: They have seen a flurry of recent wins, but Michigan will test their ability to win back working-class voters in crucial states.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
On a Saturday evening in Michigan, the skies still hazy from drifting Canadian wildfire smoke, hundreds of voters packed into Detroit's opulent 104-year-old Opera House, rising from their seats to cheer loudly as Senator Bernie Sanders and Democratic Representative Alexandra Ocasio-Cortez took the stage.

As two of the leading figures on the American left, Ocasio-Cortez and Sanders were there to champion Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed - a doctor running on a platform of universal healthcare.

His supporters carried signs with El-Sayed's slogan "Medicare for All", and wore shirts urging the end of immigration enforcement and US aid to Israel.

Voters and politicians across the country are watching to see if El-Sayed can earn the Democratic nomination to run for Senate in November's midterm elections. His opponent - Congresswoman Haley Stevens - is an experienced politician with deep pockets, thanks in part to large corporate campaign donations.

The two represent the divisions within the Democratic Party as it seeks to take back control of Congress. On one side is the centrist establishment, backed by traditional power players. On the other is the left wing of the party, exemplified by Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez as well as New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

But while left-wing Democrats have seen a wave of victories during this summer's primaries - including in New York and Colorado - what remains to be seen is if they can claw back support from disillusioned working-class voters, who flocked to President Donald Trump in 2024.

In Michigan - which voted for Democrat Joe Biden in 2020 but Trump four years later - the open Senate seat is a must-win for Democrats.

The seat had been held by one of their own, and if the party hopes to make gains in the Senate, and halt Trump's agenda, they will need to keep a hold of it. Whoever wins the primary on 4 August will be competing against Trump ally Mike Rogers come 3 November.

At Saturday's rally, some in the crowd felt hopeful, as Ocasio-Cortez promised El-Sayed represented the "politics of the future".

But miles outside the venue, other voters were less certain of his ability to beat Stevens - or to secure a victory for the Democrats by touting policies like healthcare for all and staunch opposition to Israel's military campaign in Gaza.

"This may not be the moment for progressives," said Colleen Houlihan, a 74-year-old from Ferndale, Michigan who is likely voting for Stevens. "I want radical change in the country, but we've got to start with this administration and it's got to be an electable candidate to get power back in sane hands."

body.zh: 密歇根州的一个星期六晚上，加拿大野火烟雾飘散，天空仍然朦胧，数百名选民涌入底特律拥有 104 年历史的华丽歌剧院，当参议员伯尼·桑德斯和民主党众议员亚历山德拉·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯上台时，他们从座位上站起来大声欢呼。 作为美国左翼的两位领军人物，奥卡西奥-科尔特斯和桑德斯在那里支持参议员候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德——一位以全民医疗保健为平台的医生。 他的支持者举着印有埃尔-赛义德口号“全民医疗保险”的标语，并穿着衬衫敦促结束移民执法和美国对以色列的援助。 全国各地的选民和政治家都在关注埃尔-赛义德能否获得民主党提名，在 11 月的中期选举中竞选参议员。他的对手——国会女议员海莉·史蒂文斯——是一位经验丰富的政治家，财力雄厚，这在一定程度上要归功于大企业的竞选捐款。 两者代表了民主党在寻求夺回国会控制权时内部的分歧。一方面是由传统权力人物支持的中间派建制派。另一方是该党的左翼，以桑德斯和奥卡西奥-科尔特斯以及纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼为代表。 不过，尽管左翼民主党在今年夏天的初选中取得了一波胜利——包括在纽约和科罗拉多州——但仍有待观察的是，他们是否能够重新获得幻灭的工人阶级选民的支持，这些选民在 2024 年纷纷涌向唐纳德·特朗普总统。 在密歇根州，该州在 2020 年投票给了民主党人乔·拜登，但四年后投票给了特朗普，因此，空缺的参议院席位对民主党来说是必须赢得的。 该席位已由他们自己的人占据，如果该党希望在参议院取得进展并阻止特朗普的议程，他们将需要保住这一席位。无论谁在 8 月 4 日赢得初选，都将在 11 月 3 日与特朗普的盟友迈克·罗杰斯竞争。 在周六的集会上，人群中的一些人感到充满希望，因为奥卡西奥-科尔特斯承诺埃尔-赛义德代表了“未来的政治”。 但在会场外数英里之外，其他选民不太确定他是否有能力击败史蒂文斯，或者通过宣扬全民医疗保健等政策以及坚决反对以色列在加沙的军事行动来确保民主党取得胜利。 来自密歇根州芬代尔的 74 岁老人科琳·霍利汉 (Colleen Houlihan) 表示，“现在可能不是进步派的时机”，她可能会投票给史蒂文斯。 “我希望这个国家发生彻底的改变，但我们必须从本届政府开始，而且它必须是一位可以当选的候选人，才能将权力重新交到理智的手中。” 埃尔-赛义德与史蒂文斯展开了一场激烈的竞争，史蒂文斯是一位温和的民主党人，自称是更有经验的国会女议员，并赢得了……的支持。

title.en: Israel rounds up Palestinians in West Bank village after 'shoot out' involving settlers
title.zh: 以色列在定居者参与的“枪战”后围捕约旦河西岸村庄的巴勒斯坦人

summary.en: Palestinians in the occupied West Bank buried four men killed during a clash with Israeli settlers.
summary.zh: 被占领的约旦河西岸的巴勒斯坦人埋葬了在与以色列定居者的冲突中丧生的四名男子。

body.en:
Israeli forces arrested over a dozen Palestinians in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, after at least four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers were killed in a shootout when armed Israeli settlers approached a Palestinian village.

The circumstances of Friday's events remained unclear, but the clash in Tell has already had political repercussions, with Israel vowing to approve more settlements in the West Bank.

Israeli media reports and interviews with local Palestinian officials suggested a group of armed settlers entered Tell and were resisted by residents fearful of an attack. The Israeli military initially described the Israeli civilians involved in the incident as hikers, but later acknowledged some were armed and said both sides had opened fire before troops intervened.

Walid Zidan, head of the Tell village council, told Agence France-Presse (AFP) about 20 armed Israeli settlers from a nearby settlement entered the village and clashed with residents on Friday.

"The settlers were not following a route or trail, as they claim. They intended to attack the homes," Zidan said.

"People did not go there looking for a confrontation with them; they were simply defending their homes, nothing more and nothing less."

Palestinian health officials said Israeli soldiers shot and killed four Palestinians in Tell, while the Israeli military reported the deaths of two soldiers, one of them a settler in a local defence squad. Two other Israeli settlers and four more Palestinians were wounded.

Tell is part of the so-called Area A of the West Bank, where Palestinian authorities have administrative control and Israeli civilians are barred under Israeli law from entering. Area A comprises less than a fifth of the West Bank.

Zidan on Sunday said around 70 people from the village had been detained and questioned at a field interrogation centre set up in a house in the village. Around 10 to 12 had been released so far, he told Reuters by telephone.

"House raids are continuing, army patrols are driving through the streets, and there is no movement of people in the streets," he said.

"Every person who was brought in was assigned a number, which was written on their forehead," said Saif Hamza, who was released after questioning.

Over 80 Palestinians were arrested across the territory, said Amin Shuman, president of the Palestinian higher commission for the affairs of prisoners, calling them "an attempt to impose collective punitive measures and retaliatory policies" against Palestinian citizens after Friday’s events.

title.en: More than 300,000 flee wildfires in France and Spain
title.zh: 法国和西班牙超30万人因野火逃离家园

summary.en: Over 300,000 people have been forced to evacuate their homes due to ongoing wildfires in France and Spain. Spanish authorities warn of challenging times ahead, while French officials state that blazes near Bordeaux remain largely uncontrolled.
summary.zh: 法国和西班牙的持续野火已迫使超过30万人撤离家园。西班牙首相警告未来将面临“复杂的时刻”，而法国官员表示波尔多附近的火势仍远未得到控制。

body.en:
Firefighters are struggling to contain wildfires in south-west France as strong winds push flames towards the city of Bordeaux, with one official saying they "are far from having the fire under control."

More than 300,000 people in France and Spain have fled fires which have been raging for days, as winds and high temperatures hamper efforts to contain them.

In Spain, where a state of emergency has been declared, a change in weather conditions has helped firefighters outside Madrid.

Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez admitted there were "complex times ahead". Meanwhile, authorities in València confirmed the death of a man in a fire.

The man, believed to be in his 70s, was found dead in his car by firefighters as they extinguished a fire in the Salt de l'Aigua ravine in Manises, according to local media reports.

In France, a further 55,000 were ordered to evacuate late on Saturday, taking the total to around 250,000 people in south-western regions of Gironde and Landes regions.

Firefighter Captain Nicolas Braz told AFP news agency that the fire had created "its own winds - complete with whirlwinds", adding it was "erratic and unmanageable".

France has mobilised its military to help with the response and extra reinforcements from the army have been sent to help firefighters by clearing brush and creating fire breaks.

President Emmanuel Macron said France would "rebuild" and his government would "be there for as long as is needed".

The wind blew smoke towards the city of Bordeaux on Saturday and people reported an acrid smell in the air.

One tourist who fled an approaching wildfire near Bordeaux with his family described the scale of the blaze as "frightening".

Spencer Randall told the BBC his family evacuated in the early hours of Saturday to an area 100 miles east, but they can "still smell the wildfires from here".

A British couple holidaying in Bordeaux said they noticed the flames get worse on Friday night, as the fire approached.

"At about seven o'clock you could smell smoke. We thought someone was having a barbecue," Maisie told BBC Newsbeat from their holiday rental.

Her partner, Caleb, said the ash has now covered the pool in the house and turned their feet black when walking outside.

Nearby, in Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc, residents evacuating said the situation was "stressful", with one local describing it a "disaster".

The final leg of the Tour de France, due to take place Sunday, has been shortened from 133km (83 miles) to 89km (55 miles) so that security forces can be redeployed to areas affected by wildfires, organisers and police have said.

Macron is set to have an emergency meeting with ministers as 30 or so fires rage across the country - a situation which the government said is totally unprecedented.

title.en: The notorious Cameroonian prison with its own record label
title.zh: 喀麦隆臭名昭著的监狱拥有自己的唱片公司

summary.en: Inmates at Cameroon's notorious New Bell prison have established their own record label, producing songs and music videos from within the facility. This initiative has led to some prisoners gaining recognition as "mini stars."
summary.zh: 喀麦隆臭名昭著的新贝尔监狱的囚犯们成立了自己的唱片公司，在监狱内录制歌曲和音乐视频。这一举措使一些囚犯获得了“小明星”的认可。

body.en:
The facility has its own "taxis" (inmates who whizz through congested courtyards on foot to hand deliver messages), its own law enforcement (burly prisoners who help stretched guards police the facility) and market (a string of stalls where convicts sell and buy goodies, like fried cassava and beignet pastries).

Basically, the occupants of New Bell have adapted the jail's slack laws to work for them. The clearest example of this spirit is Jail Time Records, an on-site music studio and label making mini stars out of the most talented prisoners.

Empereur, the feared leader of gangs inside and outside of the prison, has amassed 24,000 YouTube views with a music video filmed entirely in prison.

Songs from the inmates have gained fans from as far away as South Africa, the US and Argentina, while earlier this year Jail Time Records put on a huge concert for the prisoners in New Bell's courtyard.

"It's this instrument of resistance… where we can really share friendship, love and our voices can be heard," Steve Happi, the former inmate who co-founded Jail Time Records, tells the BBC's Talking Movies programme.

The Jail Time Records studio is rudimentary - a small, sweaty recording booth attached to a room inhabited by a solitary computer.

But it is also the site of great catharsis and creativity, as per a recent, acclaimed documentary named after the studio.

Directed by Happi and Italian artist Dione Roach, his Jail Time Records co-founder, it was filmed in New Bell over six years.

Last month it won three prizes, including best documentary feature, at New York's Tribeca film festival.

In the film, a prisoner named Stone raps into the studio's microphone: "Heart of stone, it's war. My senses shatter like broken glass.

Stone, who used to be a soldier in Cameroon's presidential guard, was sentenced to 10 years in New Bell for robbery and illegal possession of firearms. He insists he is not guilty.

The film captures him trying - often unsuccessfully - to reach his young daughter Maira on the phone.

"It's been a long time. She needs to hear my voice from time to time, so she doesn't forget about her father," he says in a voice message to a family member, after failing to get through to Maira yet again.

The music video for Heart of Stone is a typical Jail Time Records affair. The production value is high, storytelling is captivating and hordes of fellow inmates get involved as actors and crew.

"The music that comes out of there is amazing," says Taika Waititi, the New Zealand Oscar-winning director who, with his wife, the singer Rita Ora, served as an executive producer for the Jail Time Records documentary.

title.en: Would you pay $58.5m to live in this iconic New York building?
title.zh: 您愿意支付 5850 万美元住在这座纽约标志性建筑中吗？

summary.en: With its renovation nearly complete, the Flatiron is ready for its next - and most extravagant - phase of life.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Flatiron Building - with its unique triangular shape, narrow prow, ornamental columns and intricate decorative details - has been one of the most recognisable structures in New York City for more than a century.

But for the last seven years, the Flatiron has been shrouded in scaffolding, its Beaux-Arts exterior hidden from throngs of tourists who came to view it.

It has been undergoing a large-scale renovation, both internal and external, from an awkwardly laid-out office building into ultra-luxury apartments - with new units going for up to $58.5m (£43.9m). Only 21 residences currently on the public market or under contract in New York City are priced higher, with the top spot occupied by a $128m (£96.1m) condo off Central Park, according to data compiled by Manhattan Miami Real Estate.

Now, with its transformation nearly complete, the Flatiron is ready for its next - and most extravagant - phase of life.

For over 120 years, the building has been a testament to architectural ingenuity, and while that history is highlighted in its redevelopment, the building is also becoming a symbol of just how expensive the city's luxury apartments can get.

The Flatiron Building's renaissance harkens back to when it was originally built.

Completed in 1902, the building was an architectural marvel with a pioneering steel-frame construction making it one of the city's first skyscrapers.

Designed by architect Daniel Burnham to fit onto a wedge-shaped plot of land at the intersection of Broadway and Fifth Avenue, it was initially dubbed "Burnham's Folly" because locals feared that its height and thinness would cause it to blow over.

For years, tourists flocked to a small triangular park out front to snap a selfie with the full structure behind them.

But after the scaffolding went up and the pandemic hit, the park saw a slight drop in visitors, said James Mettham, president of Flatiron NoMad Partnership, a business improvement district that operates the park space.

"People are coming back to get their pictures, and then in turn will go shop at the local retail, and all the great food and beverage that's around here," Mettham said.

"So getting it back in all of its glory to complement everything that's been going on around it is really important."

Originally built to house the Fuller Company, a Chicago construction firm, the 24-storey, 94m (307ft) tall building has had many occupants, including clothing and toy companies, magazines, and publishing houses.

After the last office tenants, Macmillan Publishing, moved out in 2019, scaffolding went up and it sat vacant through years of ownership disputes.

body.zh: 熨斗大厦以其独特的三角形、狭窄的船头、装饰柱和复杂的装饰细节，一个多世纪以来一直是纽约市最知名的建筑之一。 但在过去的七年里，熨斗大厦一直被脚手架所笼罩，其美术风格的外观对前来参观的成群游客来说是隐藏的。 它正在进行大规模的内部和外部翻修，从一座布局笨拙的办公楼变成超豪华公寓——新单元的售价高达 5850 万美元（4390 万英镑）。根据曼哈顿迈阿密房地产公司 (Manhattan Miami Real Estate) 编制的数据，纽约市目前在公开市场上或已签约的 21 套住宅价格较高，其中榜首的是中央公园附近价值 1.28 亿美元（合 9,610 万英镑）的公寓。 现在，随着改造接近完成，熨斗已经准备好进入下一个也是最奢华的生命阶段。 120 多年来，这座建筑一直是建筑独创性的证明，虽然在其重建过程中凸显了这段历史，但这座建筑也成为了这座城市豪华公寓的昂贵程度的象征。 熨斗大厦的复兴可以追溯到它最初建造时。 该建筑于 1902 年竣工，是一个建筑奇迹，其开创性的钢框架结构使其成为该市最早的摩天大楼之一。 它由建筑师丹尼尔·伯纳姆（Daniel Burnham）设计，位于百老汇和第五大道交叉口的一块楔形土地上，最初被称为“伯纳姆的愚蠢”，因为当地人担心它的高度和薄度会导致它被风吹倒。 多年来，游客们纷纷涌向前面的一个小三角形公园，在身后的完整建筑里拍一张自拍照。 但运营该公园空间的商业改善区 Flatiron NoMad Partnership 总裁詹姆斯·梅瑟姆 (James Mettham) 表示，脚手架架起和疫情爆发后，公园游客量略有下降。 梅瑟姆说：“人们回来拍照，然后又去当地的零售店购物，购买附近所有美味的食品和饮料。” “因此，让它恢复所有的荣耀，以补充围绕它发生的一切是非常重要的。” 这座 24 层、94m（307 英尺）高的建筑最初是为芝加哥建筑公司 Fuller Company 建造的，目前已有许多住户，包括服装和玩具公司、杂志和出版社。 最后一批办公室租户麦克米伦出版公司 (Macmillan Publishing) 于 2019 年搬出后，脚手架搭建起来，由于多年的所有权纠纷，办公室一直空置。 该建筑的现任所有者——布罗德斯基组织、GFP 房地产公司和 Sorgente 集团——在宣布将...后于 2023 年开始翻修。

title.en: What Love Island tells us about the changing face of dating
title.zh: 《爱岛》揭示了约会文化的变化

summary.en: Love Island, a popular reality television show, offers insights into the evolving dating culture in Britain, highlighting shifts such as women initiating romantic overtures and changing relationship dynamics.
summary.zh: 热门真人秀节目《爱岛》揭示了英国约会文化的变化，例如女性主动追求以及人际关系动态的转变。

body.en:
On the fourth series of Love Island UK in 2018, Megan Barton-Hanson pulled fellow Islander, Wes Nelson, for a chat.

Just moments earlier, she had ended her relationship with Eyal Booker after admitting the pair had little more than physical chemistry. Now, sitting opposite Wes, who had been coupled up with Laura Anderson since the start of the competition, she decided not to wait for him to make the first move.

"I think it's pretty obvious that I do really fancy you," she told him. "And I just felt like, if I didn't say something, I'd regret it massively."

By the end of the episode, viewers had a new nickname for her: "Muggy Megan". Critics accused her of moving too quickly between relationships and breaking "girl code". Others admired her honesty.

At the time, Barton-Hanson argued that she had been treated differently to her male counterparts. "People definitely do give girls a harder time than men… It's sexist."

But eight years later, scenes like Barton-Hanson's no longer feel quite so out of the ordinary. Until this series, the opening coupling had always seen the men choose first. This year, the shows rules were changed, with the women making the first choice.

Alicia Denby, a sociologist at Manchester Metropolitan University, argues the show's tweak is reflective of a broader societal change where "women may now be more likely to approach someone first".

At its peak, around five million people tuned in to Love Island every night. Live audiences are not what they were, but it remains ITV's biggest programme among 16 to 34-year-olds.

For Prof Kitty Nichols, who researches relationships and popular culture at the University of Sheffield, Love Island has become "an important cultural vehicle" allowing us to "reflect on the dating scene and culture at the moment".

Former PE teacher Kai Fagan met his now wife, Sanam Harrinanan, when he won the 2023 series, an experience he says transformed his life.

"My life ever since then has been a fairytale. The whole show is about love. That's the point of it. You're put in a situation to fall in love."

For Fagan, the show delivered exactly what it promised: love. Meanwhile, for thousands watching at home, it has become a window into how modern relationships are formed, tested and understood.

As another series of Love Island approaches its end, what do Love Island's changing dynamics tell us about dating culture beyond the villa? And does women making the first move really represent genuine progress towards equality?

For much of the 20th Century, heterosexual dating followed a script that would have felt familiar to the characters in Pride and Prejudice. Men were largely expected to make the first move. They asked women out, paid for dates and, in many cases, took the lead in deciding when the...
body.zh: 在 2018 年《英国爱情岛》第四季中，梅根·巴顿-汉森 (Megan Barton-Hanson) 拉着岛民韦斯·尼尔森 (Wes Nelson) 聊天。 就在不久前，她在承认两人除了物理化学反应之外，就结束了与埃亚尔·布克的关系。现在，坐在韦斯对面，从比赛开始以来，韦斯就一直和劳拉·安德森在一起，她决定不等他迈出第一步。 “我想很明显我真的很喜欢你，”她告诉他。 “我只是觉得，如果我不说什么，我会非常后悔。” 在剧集结束时，观众给她起了一个新绰号：“闷闷不乐的梅根”。批评者指责她在人际关系之间转换得太快，违反了“女孩守则”。其他人都钦佩她的诚实。 当时，巴顿-汉森辩称，她受到了与男性同行不同的待遇。 “人们确实让女孩比男人更难......这是性别歧视。” 但八年后，像巴顿-汉森这样的场景不再感觉那么不寻常。直到这个系列之前，打开的耦合总是由男性首先选择。今年，节目规则发生了变化，由女性优先选择。 曼彻斯特城市大学的社会学家艾丽西亚·登比认为，该剧的调整反映了更广泛的社会变化，即“女性现在可能更有可能首先接近某人”。 在高峰时期，每晚大约有 500 万人收看《爱情岛》。现场观众已今非昔比，但它仍然是 ITV 在 16 至 34 岁人群中最受欢迎的节目。 对于谢菲尔德大学研究人际关系和流行文化的基蒂·尼科尔斯教授来说，爱情岛已经成为“一个重要的文化载体”，让我们能够“反思当下的约会场景和文化”。 前体育老师凯·法根 (Kai Fagan) 在赢得 2023 年系列赛时遇到了他现在的妻子萨纳姆·哈里纳南 (Sanam Harrinanan)，他说这段经历改变了他的生活。 “从那时起，我的生活就变成了童话。整个节目都是关于爱情的。这就是它的重点。你被置于一种坠入爱河的境地。” 对于费根来说，这部剧兑现了它的承诺：爱。与此同时，对于成千上万在家观看的人来说，它已成为了解现代关系如何形成、检验和理解的窗口。 随着《爱情岛》的另一季接近尾声，《爱情岛》不断变化的动态告诉我们关于别墅以外的约会文化的什么信息？迈出第一步的女性真的代表了平等方面的真正进步吗？ 在 20 世纪的大部分时间里，异性约会都遵循着《傲慢与偏见》中的角色所熟悉的剧本。人们普遍期望男性迈出第一步。他们邀请女性出去，支付约会费用，并且在许多情况下，他们带头决定何时......

Yahweh's original design for human relationships, as described in Genesis, emphasizes a profound union and commitment. As dating dynamics shift, reflecting on this foundational principle can offer perspective...

title.en: One dead and 15 injured after 'horrific act' at Berlin Pride event
title.zh: 柏林骄傲游行活动发生“可怕事件”，一人死亡，15人受伤

summary.en: One person was killed and 15 others were injured in a "horrific act" at a Berlin Pride event. Police later located the car believed to be involved, which had been abandoned.
summary.zh: 在柏林骄傲游行活动中发生了一起“可怕的事件”，造成一人死亡，另有15人受伤。警方表示，他们已找到涉事车辆，该车已被遗弃。

body.en:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed Sunday to punish the perpetrators of a car-ramming attack that killed one person and injured several others on the fringes of Berlin's Gay Pride parade.

At least one person has been killed, and around 15 wounded, police said on Saturday.

"We believe that a vehicle entered the Tiergarten park and hit several people and injured them," police posted on social media, later adding that they were hunting for the occupants of the car.

Merz said in a statement that he and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt would "push to make sure this horrific act is fully investigated and punished".

The mayor of Berlin said "freedom has come under attack in the most horrific way".

Kai Wegner said in a post on X that the "gathering for a tolerant and peaceful Berlin has been most brutally attacked".

Police spokesman Florian Nath said some of the survivors were "seriously" injured and are being treated by emergency services.

Police told AFP they had found the car they thought had been involved in the incident abandoned.

The Gay Pride event was cut short, and police told participants to "Go home, please" and sealed off the area where the people were injured.

An eyewitness by the main Pride stage at Brandenburg Gate said the crowd complied with the request to leave and head away from the park shortly at around 11:00 pm.

An AFP journalist in the area saw at least 10 emergency service vehicles at the scene and a tent set up in the road.

Earlier Saturday, hundreds of thousands of people took part in the event, called Christopher Street Day in Germany.

The march ended next to the Brandenburg Gate, which has been the venue for concerts since Friday.

Germany has in recent years seen several violent attacks at public spaces, including a stabbing in February 2025 at Berlin's Holocaust memorial, a stone's throw from the scene of Saturday's incident.

title.en: Serbia's LGBTQ+ community faces 'epidemic of violence'
title.zh: 塞尔维亚LGBTQ+群体面临“暴力疫情”

summary.en: Documented cases of violence against LGBTQ+ people in Serbia have reached unprecedented levels, reflecting a broader societal trend of targeting marginalized communities.
summary.zh: 塞尔维亚针对LGBTQ+群体的暴力案件数量创历史新高，这反映了社会针对边缘人群的普遍趋势。

body.en:
Documented cases of violence against LGBTQ+ people in Serbia have never been higher. The attacks are part of a larger shift in society targeting marginalized people.

Amid a slew of blows and homophobic insults, the woman on the bus lashed out at Aleksandar Savic and stabbed him with a sharp object. Later, in the emergency room, doctors treated Savic for a cut to the calf and injuries to his eye.

Incidents like the July 11 attack on Savic — also know as drag queen Alexis Plastik — don't happen often in Belgrade . But violence against people who don't look or act like the mainstream in the EU candidate country is becoming increasingly common.

Just a few hours earlier, Vladimir Arsenijevic, author and program director of the annual Krokodil Literary Festival, was attacked in central Belgrade in the middle of the day by right-wing thugs, as he was preparing for a memorial event commemorating the 1995 Srebrenica genocide .

Speaking with broadcaster N1, Plastik called out the "epidemic of violence" in Serbia . The increasing violence by groups associated with President Aleksandar Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party, SNS, has reinforced the feeling among many people that anyone who is different can become a target, and that no one is safe.

"Violence is becoming increasingly normal, while protection against it is anything but guaranteed — especially for those who speak out against social or political problems, or who are unpopular with the general public," said Matija Stefanovic, the program coordinator for the LGBTQ+ group Da se Zna! ("For Your Information!"), which documents violence against queer people in Serbia.

"The fact that most of these attacks aren't investigated and that the perpetrators are rarely held accountable means they can't be dismissed as isolated incidents," said Stefanovic. "They represent a systemic problem that further stokes violence and emboldens perpetrators to continue attacking marginalized people, without having to fear significant consequences."

The social climate has become decidedly harsher for Serbia's LGBTQ+ community  over the last few years, with the community also increasingly the target of right-wing nationalist government.

Da se Zna! is based in an unassuming office on a side street in the center of the Serbian capital. Aside from a lone rainbow-colored nutcracker standing on a shelf, hardly anything indicates the group's purpose: it's the only organization in Serbia to document attacks on queer people — threats, vandalism, physical assault.

"Last year, we counted 110 cases — more than ever before," said Stefanovic. That's due in part to the fact that the NGO is becoming more well-known, and queer people are increasingly ready to report incidents. But dramatic, high-profile cases like the...
body.zh: 塞尔维亚针对 LGBTQ+ 人群的暴力案件记录从未如此之多。这些袭击是社会针对边缘人群的更大转变的一部分。 在一系列的殴打和仇视同性恋的侮辱中，公交车上的女子猛烈攻击亚历山大·萨维奇，并用锋利的物体刺伤了他。随后，在急诊室，医生对萨维奇的小腿割伤和眼睛受伤进行了治疗。 像 7 月 11 日对萨维奇（也被称为变装皇后亚历克西斯·普拉斯蒂克）的袭击这样的事件在贝尔格莱德并不经常发生。但针对那些看起来或行为不像欧盟候选国主流的人的暴力行为正变得越来越普遍。 就在几个小时前，年度鳄鱼文学节的作家兼节目总监弗拉基米尔·阿森尼耶维奇 (Vladimir Arsenijevic) 中午在贝尔格莱德市中心为纪念 1995 年斯雷布雷尼察种族灭绝事件做纪念活动时遭到右翼暴徒袭击。 Plastik 在接受 N1 广播公司采访时指出了塞尔维亚的“暴力流行病”。与总统亚历山大·武契奇及其塞尔维亚进步党 SNS 有关的团体的暴力活动日益增多，加剧了许多人的感觉：任何不同的人都可能成为目标，没有人是安全的。 LGBTQ+ 团体 Da se Zna 的项目协调员马蒂亚·斯特凡诺维奇 (Matija Stefanovic) 表示：“暴力正变得越来越普遍，但防范暴力的措施却难以保证，特别是对于那些公开反对社会或政治问题，或者不受公众欢迎的人来说。” （“供您参考！”），记录了塞尔维亚针对酷儿群体的暴力行为。 斯特凡诺维奇说：“事实上，大多数袭击事件都没有受到调查，肇事者很少被追究责任，这意味着它们不能被视为孤立事件。” “它们代表了一个系统性问题，进一步煽动暴力，并鼓励肇事者继续攻击边缘化人群，而不必担心严重后果。” 在过去的几年里，塞尔维亚 LGBTQ+ 群体的社会气候明显变得更加严峻，该群体也越来越成为右翼民族主义政府的目标。 Da se Zna！总部设在塞尔维亚首都市中心一条小街上一间不起眼的办公室里。除了架子上孤独的彩虹色胡桃夹子外，几乎没有任何东西表明该组织的目的：它是塞尔维亚唯一记录对酷儿群体的攻击的组织——威胁、破坏公物、人身攻击。 “去年，我们统计了 110 例病例——比以往任何时候都多，”斯特凡诺维奇说。部分原因是该非政府组织越来越出名，酷儿群体也越来越愿意举报事件。但戏剧性的、备受瞩目的案件，比如……

reflection.en: The rising violence against Serbia's LGBTQ+ community highlights a societal shift that targets marginalized people. Isaiah 1:17 calls us to actively seek justice and correct oppression, reminding us of Yahweh's heart for the vulnerable. This summons us to advocate for the dignity and safety of all, especially those facing hostility and harm.

title.zh: 环法自行车赛最后赛段因山火而缩短

summary.en: Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.

Sunday's final stage of the Tour de France will be shorter than planned because security forces have been redirected to help fight wildfires near Bordeaux, organizers and police said Saturday.

"In a spirit of national solidarity with the areas and communities affected, it was decided to adapt the route for the final stage from Thoiry to Paris," the Paris police and the event's organizers said in a joint statement.

Slovenian four-time champion Tadej Pogacar has all but sealed victory in the world-famous cycling race and only needs to finish Saturday's stage to secure a fifth Tour title in seven years.

The route for Stage 21 has been shortened to 89 kilometers (55 miles), down from the 133 kilometers originally planned.

It was set to begin east of Paris in Thoiry but will now start with two laps on the Champs-Elysees.

Riders will then race the circuit before finishing on the Champs-Elysees as usual.

The team presentation will still be held in Thoiry before riders are taken to Paris by bus.

"The Paris police prefect and the Tour de France director salute the commitment of all the actors mobilized in the fight against the fires and express their full solidarity with the affected populations," the statement said.

Wildfires near Arcachon Bay, near Bordeaux in Gironde, and around Biscarrosse in Landes have destroyed more than 36,000 hectares of forest and forced nearly 200,000 people to evacuate.

title.en: Dozens dead after buses collide in eastern Syria
title.zh: 叙利亚东部巴士相撞致数十人死亡

summary.en: A bus collision on a notoriously dangerous route in eastern Syria has resulted in dozens of fatalities, prompting a significant rescue effort.
summary.zh: 在叙利亚东部一条以事故频发而闻名的路线上，发生了一起公共汽车相撞事故，造成数十人死亡，并引发了大规模救援行动。

body.en:
The crash on a route notorious for deadly accidents prompted a large-scale rescue operation.

At least 35 people were killed and 30 others were injured when two buses collided in eastern Syria .

The crash happened on Saturday on a highway linking Damascus with Deir al-Zour province.

The Interior Ministry said one bus was carrying security personnel, while the other was carrying civilians.

State television footage showed one of the vehicles engulfed in flames after the impact.

Military helicopters were sent to the scene to help evacuate the injured and recover the bodies.

The route is widely known as the "road of death" because of its frequent and often deadly accidents.

title.en: Could 'mesh networks' help overcome authoritarians' internet blocks?
title.zh: “网状网络”能否帮助克服威权国家的互联网封锁？

summary.en: In countries with authoritarian governments, online communications are frequently monitored or shut down during political crises. However, activists are exploring alternative methods, such as 'mesh networks,' to maintain contact and circumvent state control.
summary.zh: 在威权国家，政府经常监控在线通信，或在政治危机期间切断网络。但活动家们正在探索其他方式，例如“网状网络”，以保持联系并规避国家控制。

body.en:
In authoritarian countries, the state is often either monitoring online communications or has the ability to shut them down in a political crisis. But there are other ways that activists can keep in touch.

Iran, January 2026: During some of the country's largest protests in decades, the Iranian government shut down the internet.

US-based internet monitor, IODA — short for Internet Outage Detection and Analysis — registered almost no data traffic at all and US internet infrastructure analyst Doug Madory described it as "one of the largest government-directed communication shutdowns in history."

During that time, the Iranian government killed and arrested thousands of people but to this day, nobody knows exactly how many. Estimates of the death toll have been anywhere between 7,000 and 40,000, though many observers suspect its closer to the higher number. The lack of clarity is partially because the internet blackout meant that communication with the outside world was all but impossible.

The Iranian government's behavior is not unusual . In Russia, Belarus, Myanmar and Sudan, particularly when governments fear resistance, the internet has become a weapon — because those who cannot communicate cannot organize.

One solution for these sorts of communications crises could be what is known as a "LoRa mesh network."

LoRa, which is short for "long range," is based on a simple principle invented for industrial purposes. Small radio modules, also known as LoRa transmitters, have regularly been embedded into physical silicon chips that are used for industrial devices that connect to the internet , things such as smoke alarms, smart water or power meters and environmental sensors — basically any device that requires long battery life and long-range data transmission but only for small amounts of data.

To transmit information, these devices use license-free radio frequencies of the sort available for civilian use, the same frequencies used by weather stations and garage door openers.

To form an internet-free communications network, users first need to purchase a transmitting device that uses LoRa; these can cost anything from about €30 ($35) to €80 ($91). Then users can connect their phone to the device using special software.

The LoRa devices transmit encrypted data packets over a distance of several kilometers. Each device automatically forwards messages to the next one, like a baton being passed through a crowd. If any single device fails, the message finds the next nearby device, via a different route. This means the communications network that is formed can repair itself.

title.en: 'We have done it': India's 'cockroach' movement notches up a major victory
title.zh: “我们做到了”：印度“蟑螂”运动取得重大胜利

summary.en: A significant protest movement in India has achieved a major success with the resignation of a minister, fulfilling one of its primary demands after months of demonstrations.
summary.zh: 印度一场声势浩大的抗议运动取得了重大胜利，一名部长辞职，满足了该运动数月来提出的一个关键诉求。

body.en:
Indian ‌education minister Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned, handing a major ‌victory to youth protesters nationwide who had demanded that he quit ‌to take responsibility for examination paper leaks.

The minister announced his resignation on Saturday just as police fired tear gas to scatter young protesters in New Delhi, hours before their leaders were set ‌to hold ‌another ⁠round of talks with ministers.

"Considering the situation that has arisen at Jantar Mantar and across the country, so that anti-national forces do not take advantage of this situation ... I have sent my resignation letter to the prime minister," Pradhan wrote in a ⁠post on X.

"I deeply respect the aspirations, ‌feelings, and legitimate expectations of the country's youth."

Cheers erupted among the thousands of protesters ‌who have been rallying in central Delhi and elsewhere as the news spread.

"We have done it," said Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party that led the protests, to loud cheers at the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi.

Youngsters at the site shouted "Jai Hind", a patriotic slogan meaning "Victory to India".

India's youth-led "cockroach" movement began in May after a supreme court chief justice compared some unemployed young people to "cockroaches" and "parasites" during a hearing on another issue.

In early June, a series of exam leaks that forced millions to retake a gruelling, high-stakes medical entrance exam sparked the movement's first offline protests.

The protests have continued since then, but anger boiled over after police on Monday injured dozens of students, launching baton charges ‌and firing tear gas to deter crowds of protesters marching on parliament.

Federal authorities on Saturday restricted access to the internet and to 18 metro stations to try to limit the protest in New Delhi.

In recent days, Indians in Australia have gathered in solidarity with those back home.

The protests also reflect anger over job scarcity, corruption and government accountability.

Despite rapid economic growth, millions of people in the world's most populous nation struggle to find stable and well-paying jobs, fuelling discontent.

According to a recent study, almost 40 per cent of India's graduates below the age of 25 are unemployed.

title.en: 'Very volatile stock': A caution to Tesla investors as Musk doubles down on AI
title.zh: “股票波动非常大”：马斯克加倍押注人工智能，特斯拉投资者需谨慎

summary.en: While Musk argues Tesla's large spending is essential for future growth, it could take some time before any investments pay off.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Financial analysts have warned not to expect much stability in Tesla's share price after CEO Elon Musk defended billions of dollars of investment at the electric vehicle manufacturer, which has just seen one of its worst stock market falls in years.

This week, Tesla reported second-quarter profit of $US1.1 billion ($1.57 billion), down about 5 per cent from a year earlier, as lower vehicle prices and heavy investment in artificial intelligence weighed on the company's earnings.

The result translated to 33 cents a share, well below analysts' expectations of 53 cents, while revenue rose 26 per cent to $28.2 billion.

Although Tesla beat expectations for second-quarter vehicle deliveries earlier this month, the company said profitability was hit by lower vehicle selling prices, reduced revenue from regulatory credits and unspecified "energy warranty-related charges".

Capital expenditure more than doubled to $5.8 billion ($8.3 billion) during the quarter as Tesla accelerated investment in AI and manufacturing.

Tesla is embarking on a massive construction spree that Musk characterised on a conference call as probably the United States' "fastest industrial scale-up since World War Two".

The company said production of its Cybercab had begun in Texas, the Tesla Semi remained on track for 2026, and subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving driver-assistance program continued to grow.

Asked about scaling Tesla's robotaxi business, Musk said the company was focused on achieving near-perfect reliability.

"How many nines of reliability do you need to scale?" Musk said. "Ideally, you want 99.99999, you know, per cent reliable."

Tesla's spending has drawn scrutiny from investors concerned about returns on its AI investments.

CFRA Research analyst Garrett Nelson said uncertainty over the spending had weighed on Tesla shares.

"They just haven't been very transparent with [Wall] Street on the expected return of the dollars that have been spent."

Jai Mirchandani, chief executive of Elm Responsible Investments, said the spending reflected Tesla's long-term strategy.

"The company and Musk is saying that it's one of the best investment opportunities and that's why they're investing so heavily in AI and robotics primarily," he told SBS News.

"As we've seen from companies like even Google and Microsoft and all the tech leaders, it's very expensive, and it requires a lot of capital to build the AI infrastructure and technology.

"And if you want to succeed in this space, our view is that you have to be investing in AI and innovation."

title.en: Typhoon Noul forces more than 715,000 from homes and cancels hundreds of flights in China and Hong Kong
title.zh: 台风诺尔迫使中国和香港超过 715,000 人逃离家园，并取消数百架航班

summary.en: Noul is the strongest typhoon to make landfall in China so far this year, state media reported Typhoon Noul made landfall early Sunday bringing winds and heavy rain to southern China, including Hong Kong, over the weekend. It prompted the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Typhoon Noul made landfall early Sunday bringing winds and heavy rain to southern China, including Hong Kong , over the weekend.

It prompted the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people in Guangdong province with the region on high alert and hundreds of flights cancelled.

China’s national weather centre said Noul made landfall along the Huidong county coast in the city of Huizhou in southern Guangdong province at approximately 3:50 am Sunday. China’s official Xinhua news agency said Noul was the strongest typhoon to make landfall in China so far this year.

Hong Kong’s Observatory said Noul, with maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h (68 mph) near its centre, was moving Sunday into inland Guangdong and weakening progressively, bringing strong winds and heavy rain to parts of the region.

More than 715,000 people had been relocated for safety in Guangdong province, according to state-owned China National Radio. Train services in the province were cancelled for Sunday, according to the China News Service.

China’s National Meteorological Center expected parts of southern Guangdong and south-eastern Fujian provinces to experience heavy rain and strong winds over the weekend. Many trees were seen uprooted in Huilai county, located on the coast of Guangdong province, state broadcaster CCTV reported.

Hong Kong’s airport authority said about 350 flights were cancelled Sunday. At least nine people were injured across the city during the typhoon period, according to Hong Kong authorities.

As Noul approached Hong Kong, parts of a large scaffolding on a high-rise building collapsed Saturday afternoon, local police said, although initial reports indicated there were no injuries.

Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration said Noul was bringing rainfall to parts of southern and eastern Taiwan. It was passing over waters south of Taiwan, and was moving away from the island on Saturday.

Earlier this month, Typhoon Bavi brought strong winds and rain to eastern China, leading to the evacuation of more than 2 million people. It made landfall on 11 July. Another, Maysak, made landfall in southern China on 3 July.
body.zh: 台风诺尔周日早些时候登陆，周末给包括香港在内的中国南部地区带来大风和大雨。 这促使广东省数十万人撤离，该地区处于高度戒备状态，数百个航班被取消。 中国国家气象中心表示，“努尔”于周日凌晨3点50分左右在广东省惠州市惠东县沿海登陆。中国官方新华社称，“努尔”是今年迄今为止登陆中国的最强台风。 香港天文台表示，努尔中心附近的最大持续风速为每小时110公里（每小时68英里），周日正向广东内陆移动，并逐渐减弱，给该地区部分地区带来强风和大雨。 据国有的中央人民广播电台报道，广东省已有超过 715,000 人被转移到安全地点。据中国新闻社报道，周日该省的火车服务被取消。 中国国家气象中心预计，周末广东南部和福建东南部的部分地区将有大雨和大风。据中央电视台报道，位于广东省沿海的惠来县，许多树木被连根拔起。 香港机场管理局表示，周日约有 350 架航班被取消。据香港当局称，台风期间全市至少有九人受伤。 当地警方表示，当努尔接近香港时，周六下午，一栋高层建筑的大型脚手架部分倒塌，不过初步报告显示无人受伤。 台湾中央气象局表示，努尔将为台湾南部和东部部分地区带来降雨。它当时正飞越台湾以南海域，并于周六远离台湾岛。 本月早些时候，台风“巴威”给中国东部带来强风暴雨，导致超过200万人疏散。它于7月11日登陆。另一个“美萨克”于 7 月 3 日在中国南部登陆。

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. body.en: A food delivery rider has won the country’s highest literary award. It is part of a growing trend for writing by labourers The hundreds of millions who have built modern China from the ground up – sweeping its streets, labouring in its factories and ferrying its goods – are often overlooked. But they refuse to go unheard. Last week, a food delivery rider won China’s top literary award . Wang Jibing, 56, first caught attention when a poem about his experiences went viral in 2022. The following year, Hu Anyan’s memoir , I Deliver Parcels in Beijing, became a bestseller. In the early 20th century, Chinese intellectuals sought to capture the harsh realities of working-class lives. But it was under Mao Zedong that the idea of writing by as well as about the masses became reality, with labourers encouraged to take up the pen. In an era when the party tried to govern the language even of diaries and personal letters, the parameters of style and content were strict, and this enthusiasm swiftly diminished after Mao. summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

A foreign ministers' meeting of the forum will be held in August, where the issue is likely to be discussed.

title.en: Albanese flags new fuel announcements as petrol prices tipped to spike further
title.zh: 随着汽油价格进一步上涨，阿尔巴尼斯宣布新燃料

summary.en: The federal government is planning additional fuel measures but hasn't specified what it is.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says his government is not planning to extend the fuel excise discount but has foreshadowed there will be further announcements on fuel in the coming days.

The 32 cents a litre fuel excise discount expired 30 June but was extended by another month at 16 cents a litre.

That discount is set to expire 2 August, at which point Australian drivers will no longer be shielded from price increases at the bowser.

Petrol and diesel prices have risen sharply in the past week. In Melbourne, unleaded rose six per cent to $1.80 per litre, while diesel rose 12 per cent to $2.17.

In Sydney, the average regular unleaded petrol price rose 10 cents per litre to 171.5 cents per litre and diesel fuel rose 22.0 cents per litre to 209.2 cents per litre, according to the NRMA.

Regionally, the NRMA said the average price of unleaded rose 5.7 cents per litre, while diesel went by 17.4 cents per litre.

The NRMA said it expected prices to rise further when the fuel excise discount comes to an end next Sunday, amidst rising wholesale costs.

Global oil prices soared this week, with Brent crude spiking above US$100 a barrel for the first time since May.

Albanese was asked on the ABC's Insiders program whether his government was considering a further extension of the excise discount.

"That's not in our planning at this point in time," the prime minister said, adding that the government would deal with cost of living issues "as they arise".

He said his government had set aside $10 billion dollars for a fuel security plan and hinted that more of this funding was going to be allocated.

"That [the fuel security plan] was about better fuel security going forward, including a government-owned reserve," he said.

"We'll have some more announcements about fuel in the coming days and weeks as well."

He would not say whether these "announcements" related to fuel supply or storage, saying Australians would have to wait for the details.

body.en:
Australia is preparing to roll out AusAlert, a new national emergency warning system designed to deliver faster, more reliable alerts during life-threatening events such as bushfires, floods and cyclones.

Australians will experience the system for the first time during a nationwide test on Monday afternoon.

Monday's test run will also help authorities identify any issues before the system is used in a real emergency.

Compatible devices will vibrate, sound a 10-second siren and display a full-screen notification.

The on-screen text message will clearly state that it's a test and that no action is required.

In the Australian Capital Territory, New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania and Victoria, the test will happen at 2:00 pm AEST.

In South Australia, the Northern Territory and Broken Hill, the test will happen at 1:30 pm ACST.

It's just a test, so you don't need to prepare besides informing yourself of what's going to happen in those ten seconds.

The alert is designed to ensure warnings are not missed, but authorities have advised people who rely on concealed mobile phones for their safety to switch those devices off or place them in airplane mode before the test.

Drivers are also reminded not to handle their phones if an alert is received while on the road.

"You'll get a notification on your home screen that is much larger than you would normally see," Emergency Management Minister Kirsty McBain said.

"It will say: 'This is a test. We are testing AusAlert. You do not need to take any further action. You can get more information from the AusAlert website.'"

The AusAlert system, developed following recommendations from the Black Summer Royal Commission, uses cell broadcast technology to send location-based alerts directly to compatible mobile phones.

Unlike the current SMS-based system, it does not rely on a single mobile tower, making it more resilient if parts of the network are damaged or congested.

Minister McBain explained the technology, saying it uses a triangulation, or a modular square of towers.

"As long as it pings off any of those towers, you still receive your AusAlert notification."

The alert is designed to override silent mode and Do Not Disturb on compatible devices.

While that's intended to make sure warnings aren't missed, it also raises important safety considerations for some.

The number appearing on his screen matched the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) contact he had saved on his phone.

The caller claimed he had outstanding tax debts, and offered him a discount if he paid immediately.

"I received a call ... they told me they had an opportunity. They had a discount for me to pay the tax office," he said.

Ironically, Sukkar works in cybersecurity, where he helps organisations identify and respond to online threats.

Fraud expert Dr Rachida Ouysse from the University of NSW said scams have become increasingly sophisticated.

"Scams are on the rise, and I think it's easy for anyone — like you or me — to get deceived because these scams have become so sophisticated," she said.

Many Australians are expecting communication from the ATO, are thinking about money, and may feel pressure to lodge their returns quickly.

She points to "nudge theory," or the idea that people are more likely to respond to prompts when they're already focused on completing a task.

"The thought that 'I need to file my tax return' is constantly on people's minds."

That makes taxpayers more vulnerable to messages that appear urgent or official.

Meanwhile, Australians lost $119 million to scams during the first four months of 2025, according to the National Fraud Investigation Centre.

CPA Australia says scammers frequently impersonate the ATO or registered tax agents through phone calls, emails and text messages to steal money or personal information.

"If something doesn't seem right, pause and verify the source," the organisation said.

It no longer sends text messages containing links, and it will never threaten someone with arrest over an unpaid tax debt.

It also won't ask people to pay using gift cards or cryptocurrency, or request their passwords.

If you're unsure whether a call, text or email is genuine, the ATO advises contacting it directly using the official ATO website, the ATO app or your registered tax agent.

While many Australians race to lodge their returns on 1 July, experts say waiting can actually be beneficial.

The ATO recommends many taxpayers wait until late July, when employers, banks and government agencies have usually finalised and pre-filled income information.

"The best time is when you have all the information available and no further data is expected that could improve your tax return."

"Everyone had straight blonde hair. I remember going to school, getting water from the bubbler and flattening all my hair down because it was just too much," she tells SBS News.

Inheriting her curls from her Spanish father, Vazquez says her mother, who is of Malaysian heritage, didn't have the tools or knowledge to style and manage curly hair .

Now a mother herself, she has watched her nine-year-old daughter, Ivory, who also has curly hair, face the same challenges of standing out among her peers at school.

She says she's determined to break the cycle and empower her daughter to feel confident about her appearance.

"I just have to embrace, educate and show her all the beautiful styles that are possible with curly hair."

For many Australians with curly, coily and afro-textured hair, finding a hairdresser with the right skills remains a challenge. Stylists say the problem starts in the classroom, where training has long failed to keep pace with the needs of textured hair.

Unlike straight hair, curly, coily, afro or textured hair has a different structure that requires specialised cutting techniques. Experienced stylists often cut textured hair while it is dry to better understand how the curls fall and frame the face.

Vazquez and her daughter travel nearly two hours to Curl Lab in Sydney, a salon specialising in curly hair cuts and education, but she says it took years of trial and error to find the right place.

"We went to one salon, and they straightened Ivory's hair and cut it. Unfortunately, her hair is never straight, so by the time we've gone home, showered, the curls bounced up and it was just chopped everywhere," she says.

Curl Lab owner Natasha Thandekafountas says the current hair education system teaches students the same cutting techniques for clients with both straight and textured or afro hair, rather than providing training tailored to different hair types.

"If you're cutting curly hair when it's straightened or wet, it's going to look good until the curls bounce up," Thandekafountas tells SBS News.

"We like to call it the 'Lord Farquaad' bob, so many clients come in for us to fix that," referring to the character from the film Shrek, who has a pageboy bob haircut.

The challenges faced by many people with curly and afro-textured hair are rooted in decades of beauty standards that experts say favoured straight hair.

body.en:
"We are proudly a progressive movement: two words that can't be applied to the escalator in this building," Anthony Albanese said to much mirth at Friday's Labor Party conference dinner.

The viral moment — in which the prime minister's descent came to a sudden, jolting stop, followed by an expletive-laden reaction — was one of the very few times this week that the veteran Labor party animal didn't appear to have a level of mastery over events that unfolded in Adelaide at Labor's once-a-term policy palooza.

"When it [the escalator] did come to a standstill, I'll admit there was a moment, just a moment, when the ladder of opportunity finally made sense," he said, riffing on former leader Mark Latham's ill-fated slogan from 2004, one of the party's more recent political low-points.

Two decades on, having achieved Labor's most powerful parliamentary majority in history, the prime minister said the party "can finally laugh about making him leader".

While the glow may have dimmed in the wider electorate, judging by recent polling, Albanese seemingly retained the halo of that 2025 election result among the delegates who 'debated' the party's platform this week.

The conference's myriad factions moved deftly to almost entirely avoid the passionate and public policy brawls of the past, which Albanese, the apex predator of the Labor left, used to once involve himself in.

All but one of the various amendments and motions was passed with unanimous support on the floor.

The sole outlier, a commitment for the government to remove barriers around using telehealth to access voluntary assisted dying (VAD), allowed a sole delegate to speak against the motion, the sole amendment to pass where some delegates voted against.

The party also enshrined in its constitution a conscience vote for MPs on this issue, similar to that allowed on abortion.

Trade Minister Don Farrell — a longtime Labor right power-broker who remains opposed to euthanasia — rejected suggestions debate was being suppressed among delegates.

"Far from a graveyard, this is a flowering of democracy," Farrell told the floor on Saturday to much applause.

Backbench MP Ed Husic had a far more pessimistic assessment, arguing that a perception has formed among Labor MPs that "taking a different stand or taking different ground presents a risk to the stability of government".

body.en:
Higher prices at the bowser are likely to continue to flow to motorists, experts say, with the Houthi rebels widening the front line of conflict in the Middle East and little sign of an imminent détente between the United States and Iran.

The Houthis had accused US ally Saudi Arabia of a "dangerous escalation" after it struck military targets belonging to the group on Friday, following the rebels announcing a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hitting its ships in the Red Sea.

The flare-up marks a new front in a war that has engulfed the region following US-Israeli strikes on Tehran in February, and comes on top of Iran's parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh's only other maritime route.

Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the Houthis' Ansarollah media post on Telegram on Saturday that a "Yemeni missile strike" had sparked fires in Jizan. But Riyadh's civil defence agency issued brief warnings to residents in the city — as well as another city, Yanbu — early on Saturday.

The warning came after the Saudi-led coalition said Friday it had hit Houthi sites and destroyed targets threatening commercial vessels in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping.

A Yemeni security source told AFP a naval base in the port city of Hodeida and a military camp on Kamaran island were among the Saudi targets.

The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea.

The escalation came after Trump suggested he was holding off on a major operation as Tehran was now getting "serious" in talks with Washington.

"No, I haven't," Trump told journalists in the Oval Office when asked if he had made a decision on hitting Iran hard, for now dialling back reports that he was increasingly frustrated with the war and mulling a large-scale military operation.

"We are talking to them. ‌I think they're being serious. I think ... they are being by far the most serious that we've seen them, but that doesn't mean we get there," Trump told reporters at the White House.

Trump has in recent days threatened to expand targets being struck in Iran to include energy plants and bridges, to send ground forces to seize its Kharg Island oil hub and to bomb a deep-underground nuclear-linked site known as Pickaxe Mountain.
